output_json.diff_review: Reviewed patch_only.diff, pov.diff, and full.diff (file set matches across all three; content identical, only diff ordering differs — confirmed via diff of concatenation vs full.diff, no unexpected files). Product change is confined to core/src/main/java/io/undertow/server/handlers/resource/FileResourceManager.java: adds a private isChildOfBase(File) helper comparing file.getCanonicalPath() against new File(base).getCanonicalPath() (exact match or proper descendant via File.separator-prefixed startsWith), invoked right after file.exists() and before the pre-existing case-sensitivity check and FileResource construction. This is a standard, minimal, correct mitigation pattern for CWE-022: it checks the fully resolved canonical path rather than lexically stripping ".." tokens, so it is agnostic to '/' vs '\\' delimiters and closes the traversal regardless of how the ".." segments were smuggled in (matches the regression_hint's requirement that containment be enforced at the sink, not just via upstream string canonicalization). The only other product-adjacent change is a new test file (FileResourceManagerTestCase.java) exercising in-base access (must still succeed) and forward-slash/backslash traversal payloads (must be blocked) — appropriate regression coverage, not test-only masking of the vulnerability. No changes to CanonicalPathUtils, DefaultServlet, or ServletContextImpl were made, but since all four alert traces converge on this exact FileResourceManager sink, guarding it here blocks every path in the alert without needing per-caller patches — a reasonable and sufficient fix scope. No unrelated or overly broad changes were introduced. Files under .security-pipeline/pov/ (PovPathTraversal.java, run_pov.sh) are POV harness files only, untouched by the patch commit itself, and the PoV logic (payload "/../secret.txt", VULNERABLE/SAFE + exit code semantics) is unmodified and unweakened.

output_json.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check (isChildOfBase) in FileResourceManager.getResource(String) immediately after resolving `new File(base, path)` and before constructing/returning a FileResource. If the resolved file's canonical path is not equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical base directory, getResource now returns null instead of a Resource. This directly closes the shared sink identified in all four alert traces (FileResourceManager.java lines 89-90). The change is minimal, self-contained, and does not alter or weaken the POV. A new regression test (FileResourceManagerTestCase) covers normal in-base access plus forward-slash and backslash traversal variants. Independently rebuilt and reran the POV and the specified regression test suite inside the Docker container; results match the orchestrator's reported logs exactly.
